title: Rate Review Month, Written Notice of an Increase, and the Policy Anniversary
content:
An across-the-board rate change on Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is applied in the month each year in which rates are reviewed, and only after the policyholder has had the written warning the policy requires. The policy anniversary, from which a policy year is measured, is fixed by the policy on the same terms for every plan letter.

| Policy | Rate review month | Written notice before an increase takes effect, calendar days | Policy anniversary measured from |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan A | 07 | 45 | the day and month of the policy effective date |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan B | 07 | 45 | the day and month of the policy effective date |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan D | 07 | 45 | the day and month of the policy effective date |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan K | 07 | 45 | the day and month of the policy effective date |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan N | 07 | 45 | the day and month of the policy effective date |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan G | 07 | 60 | the day and month of the policy effective date |
| Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement High Deductible Plan G | 07 | 60 | the day and month of the policy effective date |

### Notes

Rates are reviewed in month 07 on every policy in the product, so the review month never turns on the plan letter a policyholder holds.

The notice period does turn on it. Plan A, Plan B, Plan D, Plan K and Plan N require 45 calendar days of written warning before an increase takes effect; Plan G and High Deductible Plan G require 60.

The policy anniversary is the day and month of the policy effective date on every letter, so a policy that took effect on a given day and month reaches its anniversary on that same day and month in each later year.
